# Jury trial

I want to simulate a short criminal jury trial where every participant is an AI agent: a prosecutor, a defense attorney, a judge and six jurors. The prosecution has four exhibits it can offer (a CCTV still, a till receipt, a witness statement and a phone record) and the defense has two (an alibi letter and a bank statement). Each exhibit has a short description of what it shows. When one side offers an exhibit, the other side may object, and the judge then sustains or overrules the objection. An exhibit that nobody objects to, or whose objection is overruled, is admitted and the jurors get to read what it shows. A sustained objection keeps that exhibit out for good, and the jurors must never see its contents. Give the evidence phase a few rounds, then each lawyer makes a closing statement. Finally each juror votes guilty or not guilty. A guilty or a not-guilty verdict needs all six jurors to agree; anything else is a hung jury.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `verdict` — exactly "guilty", "not guilty" or "hung".
- `juror_votes` — a map from each juror's id to "guilty" or "not guilty" (null for a juror who never voted).
- `admitted_exhibits` — a list of the names of the exhibits that were admitted.
- `excluded_exhibits` — a list of the names of the exhibits kept out by a sustained objection.
- `objections_sustained` — how many objections the judge sustained.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

brief.situation: A short criminal jury trial. The prosecution and the defence each have exhibits they want the jury to see. Each evidence day a lawyer may offer an exhibit; the other side may object; the judge rules. After the evidence days both sides close, and then the jury votes.
brief.rules: Evidence days 1 to {$inputs.hearing_rounds}: each lawyer may offer at most one of their own exhibits per day. When an exhibit is offered, the other side may object or waive its objection. A waived exhibit is admitted at once, and its contents go to the jury. The judge then rules on every objection: sustain keeps the exhibit out for good (its contents are never shown to the jury), overrule admits it. After the evidence days each lawyer makes one closing statement, then each juror votes guilty or not guilty. A guilty or a not-guilty verdict requires every juror to agree; anything else is a hung jury.

roles.lawyer: You are the {$actor.side} lawyer. Offer your side's exhibits, object to the other side's exhibits when they are unreliable, and make your closing statement to the jury.
roles.judge: You are the judge. Rule on each objection: sustain keeps the exhibit out of evidence, overrule admits it. Rule even-handedly on the law and the evidence.
roles.juror: You are a juror. You see only exhibits that were admitted and the lawyers' closing statements. Weigh them and vote guilty or not guilty; the verdict must be unanimous.

hearing_rounds.label: Evidence days
hearing_rounds.description: How many rounds the evidence phase lasts.

default.name: Witness statement

default.name: Alibi letter
default.contents: A signed letter from the defendant's employer saying he was at work until 22:30.

default.name: Bank statement

brief.situation: A short criminal jury trial. The prosecution and the defence each have exhibits they want the jury to see. Each evidence day a lawyer may offer an exhibit; the other side may object; the judge rules. After the evidence days both sides close, and then the jury votes.
brief.rules: Evidence days 1 to {$inputs.hearing_rounds}: each lawyer may offer at most one of their own exhibits per day. When an exhibit is offered, the other side may object or waive its objection. A waived exhibit is admitted at once, and its contents go to the jury. The judge then rules on every objection: sustain keeps the exhibit out for good (its contents are never shown to the jury), overrule admits it. After the evidence days each lawyer makes one closing statement, then each juror votes guilty or not guilty. A guilty or a not-guilty verdict requires every juror to agree; anything else is a hung jury.

roles.judge: You are the judge. Rule on each objection: sustain keeps the exhibit out of evidence, overrule admits it. Rule even-handedly on the law and the evidence.
roles.juror: You are a juror. You see only exhibits that were admitted and the lawyers' closing statements. Weigh them and vote guilty or not guilty; the verdict must be unanimous.
